title: UN experts spotlight Pak’s atrocities against civilians

ai.summary: UN experts raised concerns about Pakistan designating the Jammu Azad Action Committee (JAAC) as a terrorist group in PoK, citing alleged state violence against protesters, deaths, and arrests since June 2026.

facts.claim: UN experts raised concerns about Pakistan designating the Jammu Azad Action Committee (JAAC) as a terrorist group in PoK
facts.quote: Six UN Special Rapporteurs on human rights have raised serious concerns over Pakistan’s designation of the Jammu Azad Action Committee (JAAC) as a terrorist organisation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), citing alleged state violence against protesters, deaths, arrests and other human rights abuses over a long period.

facts.claim: The designation coincided with the commencement of nominations for legislative assembly elections on July 27, 2026
facts.quote: According to the experts, the designation coincided with the commencement of nominations for so-called legislative assembly elections on July 27, 2026.

facts.claim: At least 96 protesters have been killed, in addition to 6 police and paramilitary personnel, since the beginning of protests in June 2026
facts.quote: At least 96 protesters have been killed, in addition to 6 police and paramilitary personnel, since the beginning of protests in June 2026 – many of them young people between the ages of 15 and 35.

facts.claim: Security forces used tear gas and batons, besides resorting to lethal force to prevent protesters from advancing
facts.quote: It added that security forces used tear gas and batons, besides resorting to lethal force to prevent protesters from advancing.

ai.background_note: UN experts highlighted human rights violations in PoK following Pakistan's designation of JAAC as a terrorist group, including deaths, arrests, and restrictions on communications.
